text:
clare: quick question — i'm sketching a per-org rate policy that does RPM + TPM + concurrency cap, but adds a short preflight check and "grace credits" bucket for brief spikes. want feedback on tradeoffs before i write the console UI.

mike: high level sounds reasonable. what's the preflight check do? reject early vs route to fallback?

clare: preflight = light-weight token check at ingress to decide route: if org under steady quotas -> normal path; if burst/spike detected -> attempt grace credits; if exhausted -> route to cheaper model pool or fail fast based on tier.

jess: how do you detect spike vs sustained? window size matters a lot for fairness.

clare: good point. proposal: two windows: short rolling (10s) for bursts, and medium (5m) for sustained. grace credits consumed from a small reservoir replenished slowly (e.g., 1 credit per minute) and can be used to allow short TPS/RPM overshoot.

sara: would grace credits be per-org only or also per-api-key? we have lots of customers with many keys.

clare: per-org primary, but we can annotate credits per-key for special partners. policy precedence: per-key overrides per-org when present.

tom: what's the concurrency cap enforcement mechanism? token bucket won't handle in-flight tokens well.

mike: we currently have an approx in-flight tracker at the router. we can enforce concurrency by checking an atomic counter per-org before forwarding to the pool. if >= cap -> either queue for X ms or route to fallback.

clare: yep. i prefer immediate routing to fallback cheap model rather than long queuing to keep tail latency low.

jess: UX: in console show "Grace credits remaining", "Burst window (10s) usage", "Sustained window (5m) RPM", and "Concurrency in-flight". alert when grace < 20%.

sara: telemetry question — how do we attribute cost for grace usage? it's still billed to the org, but we should tag those tokens for cost analytics and model selection metrics.

clare: plan: add tags on request metadata: "rate_control_reason": ["normal","grace","fallback","throttled"], and record model_variant_used. pipeline will index those for cost dashboards.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: rate-policy-preflight-v1 -> staging at 2025-04-11T14:03:00Z

mike: concern: we need to ensure policy evaluation is cheap—this hits hot path. preflight needs O(1) memops, no DB calls.

clare: agreed. implementation sketch:
```
# pseudoconfig
org_policy:
  rpm: 6000
  tpm: 100000
  concurrency_cap: 100
  grace_credits_initial: 30
  grace_replenish_rate_per_min: 1
  burst_window_sec: 10
  sustained_window_sec: 300
```
preflight logic: check rolling counters in ingestion cache (redis local slot), attempt atomic decrement of grace bucket -> if success route normal, else route fallback or return 429 depending on tier.

tom: do we allow admin override for enterprise customers to never fallback? some want hard SLA.

clare: yes; enterprise flag: prefer_queue_or_reserved_capacity. for EA accounts we skip fallback and hit reserved pool or queue for up to 200ms.

jess: also consider a smoothing factor to avoid oscillation when org flips between normal and fallback rapidly. maybe require 2 consecutive windows breaching.

mike: good call. add hysteresis: require X seconds below threshold before bringing them back.

sara: for dashboards add synthetic "expected cost with and without grace" to show unit economics.

clare: thanks. i'll write up the RFC with config DSL and a small state diagram. next steps: perf microbench of preflight on router cache and a staging canary.

mike: please include tests for race on grace decrement (concurrent requests from same org) — classic ABA.

clare: noted. i'll ping when RFC is ready. :thumbsup:
